title: Binary Search
summary: Binary search is an algorithm that finds an element in a sorted array in O(log n) time. While it appears simple, boundary handling can be tricky, and its applications extend to parametric search.

blocks.content: Binary Search is an algorithm that reduces the search range by half in a sorted array. It compares the middle value (mid) with the target value - if the target is larger, it searches only the right half; if smaller, only the left half.

While linear search checks all n elements with O(n) complexity, binary search narrows the range by half at each step, achieving O(log n). For n=1,000,000, it can find the target with at most 20 comparisons.

items: Space Complexity: O(1) for iterative, O(log n) stack for recursive
Even with n=1 billion, search completes with at most 30 comparisons

blocks.content: The core of binary search lies in three pointers: left, right, and mid. We calculate the middle index as mid = (left + right) / 2 and compare arr[mid] with the target value to narrow down the range.
Caution: left + right can cause integer overflow. The safe calculation is mid = left + (right - left) / 2. Clearly defining loop invariants can prevent boundary value errors.

items: while(left <= right): Check the exact same position too
Return immediately when found, return -1 if not found
Loop invariant: Answer exists within [left, right] range

blocks.content: 90% of binary search bugs stem from boundary handling mistakes. Whether to use while(left < right) or while(left <= right), whether to update right to mid-1 or mid - the behavior changes based on these choices.
Implementation varies based on the goal. 'Finding an exact matching element' and 'finding the first position satisfying a condition (lower_bound)' require different implementations.

items: Exact search: while(left <= right), return mid when found
lower_bound: When condition satisfied, right = mid (preserve answer candidate)
upper_bound: When condition exceeded, left = mid + 1
off-by-one: Always verify with small examples (n=2,3)

blocks.content: Beyond finding values, binary search is powerfully applied to 'optimal value search'. 'Finding minimum/maximum values that satisfy certain conditions' can be solved with binary search in O(log(range) × condition check cost).

Example: 'When cutting a rope into k pieces, each with length at least m, what's the maximum m?' This problem applies binary search on the value m, and checks condition satisfaction for each m in O(n).

items: Parametric search: Apply binary search on the answer range
Applicable when condition function f(x) is monotone
Representative problems: Cutting trees, cutting cables, crossing stepping stones
Integer range binary search: O(log N), Real number range: epsilon-based iteration
